judge.rationale: The implementation is a textbook example of Pythonic clarity and directness. It uses a single sorted set union to enumerate all fields, explicitly computes before/after values using dict.get (correctly returning None for absent fields), filters only changed fields, and builds explicit records with the required field/before/after keys. The sorting is done at the iteration level rather than as a post-processing step, and the entire logic fits in a flat, readable loop with no unnecessary abstractions, helper functions, or architectural complexity. It perfectly satisfies all SRL-3 requirements: every change is an explicit record, nothing is collapsed into summaries, and field labels are preserved exactly.
